record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: Continuous-time periodic systems are sometimes represented in a frequency-lifted form that produces large structured matrices with block Toeplitz or block Toeplitz-plus-diagonal structure. Can one develop efficient structure-exploiting or structure-preserving algorithms for computations based on this frequency-lifted representation?

evidence.quote: Some of existing computational methods employ the frequency-lifted representation of continuous-time periodic systems ... which leads to large-scale structured system matrices with block Toeplitz or block Toeplitz plus diagonal structures. Efficient structure exploiting/preserving algorithms using this representation are still missing and their development is an open field for research.

status_evidence.title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Efficient structure exploiting/preserving algorithms using this representation are still missing and their development is an open field for research.
status_evidence.claim: The development of structure-exploiting/preserving algorithms based on the frequency-lifted representation of continuous-time periodic systems is identified as an open research direction.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is identified as an open research direction. A targeted search did not surface a comprehensive solution providing structure-exploiting/preserving algorithms for the full range of periodic-systems computations in the frequency-lifted block-Toeplitz formulation; only partial work on specific tasks (e.g. harmonic transfer function truncations, harmonic Lyapunov equations) appears, so the general problem remains open.
